name_reason: Compliant with data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention: data_fd2_ (game global) + ui (domain) + player_action_menu_state_template (descriptor). Descriptor accurately reflects both purpose (per-slot enable/disable flag STATE for the player action menu) and data shape (a TEMPLATE array copied into a local before use). No Ghidra address residue (no hex suffix equal to its own or any data address). Matches the sibling *_menu_state_template family naming.
purpose: Zero-initialized template holding the per-slot enable/disable gating flags for the player's inline action submenu (Attack/Spell/Item/Wait); copied into a local stack buffer at the start of the player's turn UI, never read directly as live state.
logic_summary: int32[4], all zero (= every action slot enabled by default). Sole reader fd2_player_action_menu_loop (@0x18890) copies all 4 dwords via REP MOVSD (MOV ECX,4; MOV ESI,0x53F12; REP MOVSD) into a local menu_state[16]. On the path where the unit moved before acting (portrait_id not in {0x12,0x13,0x22}) it sets ((int*)menu_state)[1]=1 (binary: MOV dword[ESP+4],1; decompiles as menu_state[4]=1) to grey out the Spell slot, then passes the local copy to fd2_player_inline_action_menu_dispatch, which declares it int* pSlot_disable_arr and indexes [0..3] (non-zero = disabled). The global itself is never written by the game; only the local copy is mutated.
element_semantics: Per-slot gating flag for the inline action submenu, indexed by menu slot 0..3 = {Attack, Spell, Item, Wait}; element value 0 = slot enabled, non-zero = slot greyed out/disabled. Paired with data_fd2_ui_inline_action_menu_template @0x51ED5 which supplies the slot option IDs {0,1,2,3}.

issues.title: Read-only state template declared non-const (whole *_menu_state_template family)
issues.description: data_fd2_ui_player_action_menu_state_template has zero game-side write-xrefs (both xrefs are READ/DATA from fd2_player_action_menu_loop; only the local stack copy is mutated) and lives in a write=false .object2 block, so per the project const-data policy it is a true read-only table and a candidate for const. It is currently declared non-const (int32 ...[4] at uitab.c:233), as are all 5 sibling *_menu_state_template arrays (uitab.c:193/211/233/253/275). The Ghidra annotation even tags emit_action=emit_c_const_zero, corroborating const intent. Changing const-ness is a type/declaration change explicitly out of scope for this comment/name refine stage, so it is recorded only. Note the sibling const option-templates in the same file (e.g. data_fd2_ui_inline_action_menu_template) ARE already const, so the state-template family is inconsistent with them.
issues.evidence: Ghidra: block .object2 read=true write=false; xrefs_to 0x53f12 = {0x188ac DATA, 0x188b1 READ} both in fd2_player_action_menu_loop; read_memory(0x53f12,16)=all zero. src: uitab.c:233 declares 'int32 data_fd2_ui_player_action_menu_state_template[4] = {0,0,0,0};' (non-const), vs uitab.c:48 'const int32 data_fd2_ui_inline_action_menu_template[4]'. Old Ghidra PRE comment metadata: emit_action=emit_c_const_zero.

notes: src comment (uitab.c:213-233) was already thorough and fully verified against disassembly (REP MOVSD copy at 0x188a5-0x188b1; MOV dword[ESP+4],1 at 0x18a72) and against the consumer fd2_player_inline_action_menu_dispatch (signature int* pSlot_disable_arr, indexes [0..3], non-zero=disabled) -> comment_verdict=keep, no src edit. Ghidra had NO plate (PLATE_COMMENT=null) and instead a slightly-inaccurate PRE comment (called the data 'BSS' although it is an initialized zero int[4] in write=false .object2, and tagged emit_c_const_zero). Per project rule data plates must use PLATE_COMMENT not PRE_COMMENT, so created the canonical PLATE_COMMENT (concise, src-consistent) and cleared the stale PRE comment. is_const reflects ground-truth read-only status (zero game writers); the actual const-ness of the src declaration is left to Stage 2/post-workflow per the recorded issue. Staged change for this symbol = shard file only (no src diff).
